title: Public-opponent external-ranking alignment audit
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Across six exact frozen greedy policies with independent fresh20k Slumbot evidence, score versus the frozen public-state Slumbot model will preserve external ranking: Spearman at least 0.6, Kendall tau at least 0.5, positive rank direction in both seats, positive paired-bootstrap lower tail, and at least 0.75 joint probability of positive rank correlation after external measurement uncertainty.
material_change: Add an evaluation-only polymorphic frozen-policy runner for audited legacy-v4, native-v6, and dual-contract adapters. Play every policy on 4,096 common decks in both seats versus the same frozen sampled public-opponent model; retain raw pair outcomes and jointly bootstrap local deal variance plus fresh20k external score uncertainty.
baseline: Internal opponent panels have repeatedly reversed on fresh Slumbot. The public model improved session-disjoint action NLL by 34.03%, but its hero-training treatment failed; whether it is useful as an evaluation-only external-alignment proxy is unknown.
notes: This is a zero-training-hand calibration audit, not a hero-strength experiment. All six external points use untouched 20k fresh greedy evaluations, while contract-specific observation adapters remain exact. No new Slumbot calls.

All 49,152 evaluation hands completed and the gzip writer closed. The initial command then failed only while serializing a numpy.bool_ gate into summary JSON; raw outcomes, decks, checkpoint hashes, seeds, and hand counts are intact. Recovery is read-only and will not replay poker hands; decision-count telemetry was not present in raw rows and will be explicitly null.

result.summary: Six exact frozen greedy policies completed 49,152 common-deck, both-seat evaluation hands versus the frozen public Slumbot action model. External fresh20k rank alignment was strongly negative: Spearman -0.543, Pearson -0.593, Kendall tau -0.333; both seats were negative, paired bootstrap never produced positive Spearman, joint external-uncertainty probability positive was 15.8%, and only 1/9 externally decisive policy pairs was ordered correctly. Initial summary serialization failed after all raw hands, then a disclosed read-only recovery recomputed the complete result; independent audit passed all 13 evidence gates.
result.conclusion: The public model is a useful behavior-prediction artifact but an anti-aligned hero-strength proxy under policy-induced state shift. This is a matched evaluation mechanism rejection, not an undertraining result. It also explains why positive local exploitation scores cannot justify scaling public-opponent hero training.
result.next_step: Do not use this model for checkpoint selection, learning-curve admission, or resource scaling. Preserve it only for opponent-behavior analysis. Select the next learned-weight direction using evidence that does not rely on this proxy, prioritizing robust geometric curves, Standard10 preservation, multi-seed breadth, and sparse fresh Slumbot calibration.
